criteria.retire_with_register: Retire each runner once its wire legs pass live, and move every check-blocked leg into a permanent coverage register (checklist entry plus Can file header) as explicitly uncovered: named check, missing primitive, and the date it was parked. The 28-record goal completes with stated exceptions; the register, not the runners, carries the uncovered checks.
criteria.runners_stay: Keep every runner that owns a check-blocked leg indefinitely (the .mjs/.ts files keep running those legs in CI or on demand). Their Can files carry the ported wire legs plus blocked-leg records. The 28-record goal completes at 28 minus the parked records, with the parked set explicitly listed as not migrated.
criteria.substitute_narrow_property: Permit retirement only when each check-blocked leg is re-proven as a narrower live Can verdict over production behavior: e.g. instead of asserting the browser blocks a form action, assert the server emits the exact form-action CSP directive; instead of jar semantics, assert the exact set-cookie wire strings. Checks that admit no honest narrower verdict keep their runners under the runners-stay rule.

blocked_retirement.instructions: Which retirement rule should govern checks that no Can mechanism can execute, so the 28-record migration ends honestly?

state.aspect_vs_check: Two blocked kinds must stay distinct. Aspect-blocked: the underlying property IS proven in Can another way and only one aspect is unproven — e.g. A01/A02/B04 prove caps and single-use sequentially while simultaneity stays unproven; those runners already retired and that precedent stands. Check-blocked: the ENTIRE check is unproven in Can — e.g. 'Chromium reports a CSP violation' or 'the cookie jar refuses a forged __Host- cookie' have no Can execution path at all. Only check-blocked legs are at issue here.
state.blocked_inventory: The C03 probe.ts browser closer (lines 227-277, 2 groups) and about 5 of proof.mjs's 9 groups plus strict-redirect.mjs's form-action and click-chain legs depend on: JavaScript evaluation with DOM/CSS/font/media readback (getComputedStyle, fonts.ready, image decode, clicks), real cookie-jar semantics (__Host- prefix, HttpOnly, SameSite, redirect carriage, forgery refusal), CSP enforcement signals (securitypolicyviolation), navigation with default versus overridden referrers, and worker/serviceworker gating. TLS-listener serving is check-blocked on the client side (Bun fetch rejects the self-signed fixtures; verified 2026-10-02) while bind-only legs stay live.
state.gate_text: The checklist's standing gate reads: a host harness retires only when its retained legs pass as running Can verdicts against production behavior, reconciled by F01, and progress counts only fulfilled baseline obligations. The 28 records comprise 21 code files plus 3 documents plus 4 further owned artifacts; C02 owns 2 .mjs runners, C03 owns 2 .ts probes plus README.md, C04 owns 5 fixture files. S04 (approval_probe.ts) has no browser legs and is expected to retire outright.
state.mandate: Can is an AI-agent-authored language with no backwards-compatibility obligations; the standing rule prefers reaching the migration goal over scaffolding and nested proof layers. A prior Jev consultation (3/3, confidence 0.96+, 2026-10-02) selected porting all wire-observable legs with explicit blocked legs and no new runtime surface; the user confirmed. This question settles what happens to the blocked remainder.
state.precedent_pressure: Every port so far retired its runner with zero check-blocked legs (worst case: aspect-blocked simultaneity with the property proven sequentially). C02/C03 are the first queues where whole checks cannot execute in Can. Whatever rule is chosen becomes the migration's definition of done for unportable checks and will be cited at F01.
